cards: Hannibal Barca was a Carthaginian general who led the invasion of Italy during the Second Punic War.
Antiochus III the Great was a Seleucid king who reigned from 222 to 187 BCE.
Xiang Yu was a Chinese military leader who led the rebellion against the Qin dynasty and became the dominant warlord after its fall.
Liu Bang was the founder of the Han Dynasty, ruling as Emperor Gaozu from 202 BCE.
Ashoka was a Maurya emperor who ruled most of the Indian subcontinent in the third century BCE and died in 232 BCE.
Pyrrhus was a king of the Molossians and of Epirus, sheltered as an infant by the Taulantian king Glaukias.
Cleomenes III was King of Sparta from about 235 BCE.
Philip V of Macedon was Antigonid king of Macedonia from 221 to 179 BCE.
Publius Cornelius Scipio Africanus was the Roman general who defeated Carthage in the Second Punic War.
Antigonus III Doson was king of Macedon from 229 BCE.
Philopoemen was a general and statesman of Megalopolis who served eight times as strategos of the Achaean League.
Qin Shi Huang, born Ying Zheng, became king of the State of Qin in 246 BCE and between 230 and 221 BCE conquered the six rival Warring States, unifying China.
Epicurus was a Greek philosopher, born on Samos to Athenian settlers, who founded the Epicurean school.
Han Fei (c. 280–233 BCE) was a prince of the State of Han and the leading theorist of Legalism.
Antigonus II Gonatas was king of Macedon and son of Demetrius Poliorcetes.
Aratus of Sicyon was a Greek statesman who freed his city from its tyrant in 251 BCE, brought it into the Achaean League and led the league for over thirty years as its general.
Bai Qi was a general of the State of Qin in the Warring States period and one of the most successful commanders of ancient China.
Han Xin was the leading general of Liu Bang in the Chu–Han war that founded the Han dynasty.
Ptolemy II Philadelphus was king of Egypt from 283 to 246 BCE, born on Kos.
Wang Jian was a general of the state of Qin under King Zheng, the future First Emperor.
Antiochus II Theos was king of the Seleucid Empire from 261 to 246 BCE.
Eratosthenes of Cyrene was a Greek scholar who became head of the Library of Alexandria under the Ptolemies.
Hiero II of Syracuse was a general who seized power in Syracuse and took the title of king after defeating the Mamertines at the Longanus river around 265 BCE.
Livius Andronicus was a Greek from Tarentum who became the first known Latin poet and dramatist.
Manetho was an Egyptian priest of Sebennytos in the Nile Delta who wrote a history of Egypt in Greek, the Aegyptiaca, under the early Ptolemies in the 3rd century BCE.
fl. early 3rd century BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Plautus, in full Titus Maccius Plautus, was a Roman comic playwright.
Yue Yi was a general of the Warring States period who served King Zhao of Yan.
Archimedes of Syracuse was the greatest mathematician and engineer of the ancient Greek world.
Aristarchus of Samos was a Greek astronomer and mathematician of the third century BCE.
Jing Ke was a retainer of Crown Prince Dan of Yan who tried to assassinate King Zheng of Qin, the future First Emperor, in 227 BCE.
Lü Buwei was a wealthy merchant who became chancellor of the State of Qin.
Magas was ruler of Cyrene, a son of Ptolemy I's queen Berenice I by an earlier marriage.
d. c. 250 BCE · South & Southeast Asia
Prusias I was king of Bithynia from about 228 to 182 BCE.
Sophonisba was a Carthaginian noblewoman, daughter of the general Hasdrubal Gisco, who was married to King Syphax of the Masaesyli to bind him to Carthage in the Second Punic War.
Zeno of Citium was a philosopher from Kition in Cyprus who founded Stoicism.
Agis IV was a Eurypontid king of Sparta who came to the throne about 245 BCE and tried to restore the shrinking citizen body by cancelling debts and redistributing land among Spartans and selected…
Aratus of Soli was a Greek poet from Cilicia who lived at the Macedonian court of Antigonus II Gonatas.
Attalus I Soter ruled Pergamon from 241 to 197 BCE.
Bindusara was the second emperor of the Maurya Empire, son of Chandragupta Maurya and father of Ashoka.
r. c. 297–273 BCE · South & Southeast Asia
Chares of Lindos was a Greek sculptor from Rhodes, a pupil of Lysippus.
